title: The 10 Best Tin Snips
subtitle: Aviation tin snips and snip sets for sheet metal, flashing and ductwork, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: Aviation tin snips use compound leverage to cut sheet metal by hand. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Crescent Wiss, Midwest, STANLEY, CRAFTSMAN, HURRICANE and Amazon Basics on rating, review volume and features (a full left/right/straight set, an 18-gauge rating, a one-hand latch and a lifetime warranty). Start with a yellow straight-cut snip, then add red and green for curves.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: XUDYVCO 8 Inch Aviation Tin Snips with Sharp Stainless Steel Blade
avoid.flag: Sold as aviation snips; rated only to 26 gauge
avoid.verdict: It's sold as aviation snips, but the listing says it's not suitable for sheet thicker than 0.5 mm (26 gauge). Most aviation snips here cut 18 gauge.
reasons: The listing says 'Not suitable for high hardness metal sheets over 0.5mm/26 gauge', much thinner than the 18-gauge rating of the Amazon Basics, STANLEY and Wiss snips.
The blades are described as stainless steel, not the chrome vanadium or molybdenum steel used on the snips we rank.
It's rated 4.0 stars, the lowest of the snips we looked at. The Amazon Basics straight snip costs a few dollars more and is rated for 18 gauge.

buyers_guide.a: Aviation snips are color-coded. Yellow cuts straight and wide curves, red cuts left curves, green cuts right curves. If you buy one, get yellow. For ductwork and flashing, a full set saves fighting the metal.
Gauge is sheet thickness; a bigger number is thinner. 18-gauge steel is about 1.2 mm, the upper end for hand snips. Residential HVAC duct is typically in the mid-20s gauge.
Offset snips have the handles raised above the blades, so your hand stays clear of the sheet on long cuts. Pros cutting lots of duct and roofing prefer them.
Most snips here cut about 22-gauge stainless, which is harder than mild steel. Check the listing's stainless rating.

buyers_guide.q: How do I avoid cuts on my hands?
buyers_guide.a: Wear cut-resistant gloves. Sheet metal edges are razor sharp, and the waste strip curls toward you.
